source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
Soil: the thesis describes the proposed plantation site as having a clean, sandy soil layer suitable for coconut, with a groundwater table assessed as being at a workable depth for the crop's needs.

Proposed farm organizational structure for running the new plantation: a Director (នាយក) oversees two operational teams and a small admin staff. Team 1 is responsible for nursery-bed work, headed by one supervisor over 60 nursery workers. Team 2 is responsible for land preparation and planting, headed by 4 supervisors over 60 planting/land-prep workers. A separate small staff of 6 people reports directly to the Director, including one person responsible for accounting and warehouse management. In total the plan envisions roughly 131 people (1 director, 6 admin/warehouse staff, 1 nursery supervisor + 60 nursery workers, 4 planting supervisors + 60 planting workers) to establish and run the new plantation.
